claims.text: Maintaining the AlCrFeNiSi build zone at an elevated controlled temperature during deposition will reduce residual thermal stresses relative to conventional high-thermal-load laser additive manufacturing.
Maintaining the build zone at an elevated controlled temperature during deposition will improve the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components.
Preheating the build chamber and substrate to 400–600°C throughout deposition will provide an in-situ annealing environment.
Reducing steep thermal gradients will produce coarser grains in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Reducing steep thermal gradients will produce more equiaxed grains in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Reducing steep thermal gradients will lower dislocation density in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
Reducing steep thermal gradients will decrease microcracking in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed grain structure, lower dislocation density, and reduced microcracking will improve ductility.
The proposed grain structure, lower dislocation density, and reduced microcracking will improve strength.
Sustained elevated temperature during deposition will enable dynamic recovery in AlCrFeNiSi.
Sustained elevated temperature during deposition will enable partial recrystallization in AlCrFeNiSi.
Dynamic recovery and partial recrystallization will relieve accumulating residual thermal stresses.
The elevated-temperature intervention will promote a more thermodynamically favorable microstructure and reduce phase instabilities associated with rapid cooling.
The intervention will yield higher ductility than conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The intervention will yield higher tensile strength than conventional high-thermal-load processing.
The intervention will minimize post-processing corrections for thermal distortion and thereby simplify the processing regime.
Standard laser additive manufacturing of the baseline components involves high thermal gradients and rapid cooling rates.
The stated applicability is limited to miniature geometries, such as approximately 1 mm walls, made under inert atmosphere at controlled build temperatures of approximately 400–600°C.

contradictions.description: The conditions call for adjusted laser power density and scan strategy to maintain a stable build temperature, whereas the falsification experiment requires laser parameters to remain identical between groups except for controlled build temperature. These prescriptions confound whether laser settings are part of the intervention.
